title: Check yourself: MCP advanced: Streamable HTTP, state and authorization

questions.stem: An MCP server on Streamable HTTP receives a request whose Origin header shows an unrelated site. What does the specification require?

options.text: Accept it, since the Origin header is advisory and only logged
options.says: Ruled out because "Servers MUST validate the Origin header on all incoming connections to prevent DNS rebinding attacks."

options.text: Answer 403 Forbidden, which blocks DNS rebinding attacks
options.says: The page says "Servers MUST validate the Origin header on all incoming connections to prevent DNS rebinding attacks", and that an invalid one gets 403 Forbidden.

options.text: Close the stream of the next response so that the sender retries
options.says: Ruled out because "Closing the response stream is cancellation", which is how a client cancels a request, and it is not an answer to a bad Origin.

options.text: Redirect it to the authorization server so that the sender can authenticate
options.says: Ruled out because "If the header is present and invalid, the server must answer 403 Forbidden", not a redirect.

questions.stem: An MCP server accepts a credential that was meant for another service and passes it unchanged to a downstream API. What does the specification say about this behavior?

options.text: It is allowed, since the downstream API validates the token again
options.says: Ruled out because the danger is that "the downstream API trusts the call as though the MCP server had validated it", so a second validation does not make it safe.

options.text: It is allowed once the user has consented to the downstream call
options.says: Ruled out because "Token passthrough is explicitly forbidden", with no consent exception.

options.text: It is required, so the original audience stays visible downstream
options.says: Ruled out because "MCP servers MUST validate that access tokens were issued specifically for them as the intended audience", so the original audience is the receiver and not the downstream API.

options.text: It is forbidden, and onward calls need a token of its own
options.says: The page says "MCP servers MUST NOT accept or transit any other tokens." and that "If the server needs to call a downstream API, it uses a token of its own for that API."

questions.stem: A server issues a workflow identifier in a tool result and later acts on whoever presents it. Which attack does this invite?

options.text: Session fixation on a protocol-level session
options.says: Ruled out because MCP in this revision "is stateless and has no protocol-level sessions", so there is no session to fix.
The page says "MCP servers MUST NOT treat possession of a state handle as authentication."

options.text: Scope inflation through an overbroad token
options.says: Ruled out because the remedy is that "MCP servers SHOULD bind handles server-side to the authenticated user", which is about ownership and not about permissions.

options.text: Token passthrough to a downstream API
options.says: Ruled out because passthrough is "A server that accepts tokens issued for another service, or forwards the client's token to a downstream API", and a handle is not a token.
